summaryText:
Pastor Travis (also called PT in the message) continued the Build My Church series with part two, building on last week's call to pick up your hammer. This week's message was to start swinging it, and it centered on two simple words: "Yes, Lord." He explained that everything God does through people begins with someone saying yes. He pointed to the story of Impact Church, which began with a yes to start a Bible study, and to the many volunteers whose yes serves children, teens, recovery groups, and guests each week. He encouraged the church that someone else may be waiting on their yes.

He shared four thoughts under the title "Yes Lord, Use Me." First, God does not need your ability, he needs your availability. Using Moses and his excuses in Exodus 4:12, and Isaiah's response in Isaiah 6, he taught that God qualifies the called and is not looking for perfect people, only available ones. Second, your gift was never meant just for you. Using 1 Peter 4:10 and 1 Corinthians 12, he taught that every believer is blessed to be a blessing and that each person is an important part of the body of Christ, where no part can say to another, "I don't need you." Third, your yes is bigger than you think. He retold the boy with five loaves and two fish in John 6, where Jesus took what was offered, blessed it, and multiplied it. He shared his own story of saying yes at age 17 without seeing what God would do through it, and noted that many biblical figures could not see what their yes would lead to. Fourth, there is a cost to saying no. He used Jonah's running from God's call to show that our choices affect the people around us, and he lovingly challenged those who attend but do not serve to move from consuming to building.

Pastor Travis invited everyone, in person and online, to sign up for the Get in the Game membership class and to visit the booth to explore serving opportunities. He also encouraged online viewers to get involved through giving, hosting watch parties, or starting house churches. He closed in prayer, offering everyone a chance to say yes to serving, and gave those who do not yet know Christ an opportunity to give their lives to Jesus. The message ended with a call to say, "Here am I. Send me."
mainPoints: God does not need our ability, he needs our availability. He qualifies the called, so we should stop letting excuses keep us from saying "Yes, Lord."
Our gifts were never meant just for us. We are blessed to be a blessing, and every member of the body of Christ has a part to play in serving others.
Our yes is bigger than we think. Jesus multiplies what we offer, others are waiting on our yes, and saying no carries a cost for us and for those around us.

versesMentioned.text: And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overcome it.
Now go; I will help you speak and will teach you what to say.

And they were calling to one another: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD Almighty; the whole earth is full of his glory." At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook and the temple was filled with smoke. "Woe to me!" I cried. "I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the LORD Almighty." Then one of the seraphim flew to me with a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with tongs from the altar. With it he touched my mouth and said, "See, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away and your sin atoned for." Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?" And I said, "Here am I. Send me!"
Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms.
Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ.

Now if the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," it would not for that reason stop being part of the body. If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be? But in fact, God has placed the parts in the body, every one of them, just as he wanted them to be. If they were all one part, where would the body be? As it is, there are many parts, but one body. The eye cannot say to the hand, "I don't need you!" And the head cannot say to the feet, "I don't need you!" On the contrary, those parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and the parts that we think are less honorable we treat with special honor. And the parts that are unpresentable are treated with special modesty, while our presentable parts need no special treatment. But God has put the body together, giving greater honor to the parts that lacked it, so that there should be no division in the body, but that its parts should have equal concern for each other. If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
Here is a boy with five small barley loaves and two small fish, but how far will they go among so many?
Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted. He did the same with the fish.

The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai: "Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before me." But Jonah ran away from the LORD and headed for Tarshish. He went down to Joppa, where he found a ship bound for that port. After paying the fare, he went aboard and sailed for Tarshish to flee from the LORD.
Then the LORD sent a great wind on the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship threatened to break up.

Monday.scripture: Isaiah 6:8 (NIV): "Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, 'Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?' And I said, 'Here am I. Send me!'"
Monday.focus: Availability over ability: offering God a simple, open yes.
Monday.action: Write down one way you could serve this week at church, at home, or in your neighborhood. Set aside a specific time for it and put it on your calendar.
Monday.prayer: Lord, here am I. Send me. I give you my time, my hands, and my willingness. Use me however, wherever, and whenever you choose. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Exodus 4:12 (NIV): "Now go; I will help you speak and will teach you what to say."
Tuesday.focus: Setting aside excuses and trusting that God qualifies the called.
Tuesday.action: Name one excuse that has kept you from serving (time, talent, or experience). Write it on paper, pray over it, and take one small step toward serving anyway.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, I lay down my excuses today. I trust that your ability is greater than mine. Thank you for going with me. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: 1 Peter 4:10 (NIV): "Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms."
Wednesday.focus: Your gifts were given to bless others.
Wednesday.action: List three gifts, skills, or experiences God has given you. Choose one and use it today to help or encourage someone else.
Wednesday.prayer: God, thank you for the gifts you have entrusted to me. Show me who needs them today, and help me be a faithful steward. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: 1 Corinthians 12:27 (NIV): "Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it."
Thursday.focus: Every part matters in the body of Christ.
Thursday.action: Encourage someone who serves at church by sending a short thank-you message. Then ask a church leader or friend where help is needed.
Thursday.prayer: Jesus, thank you for making me part of your body. Help me value every member and do my part with joy. Amen.

Friday.scripture: John 6:11 (NIV): "Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted. He did the same with the fish."
Friday.focus: Giving Jesus what you have, even if it feels small.
Friday.action: Choose one small thing to give this week, such as an hour of your time, a smile at the door, a prayer for a neighbor, or a generous gift. Offer it to God and trust him with the result.
Friday.prayer: Lord, I do not have much, but I give you what I have. Take it, bless it, and multiply it for your glory. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Jonah 1:1-2 (NIV): "The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai: 'Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before me.'"
Saturday.focus: Answering God's call instead of running from it, knowing our yes affects others.
Saturday.action: Think about whether God has been nudging you toward something you have been putting off. Take one concrete step today, such as signing up for the Get in the Game membership class, visiting the serve booth, or reaching out to a ministry leader.
Saturday.prayer: Lord, I do not want to run from your call. Give me courage to say yes before I know everything on the other side of it. Use me to build your church. Amen.

title: GOD CAN USE YOU. YES, YOU.
